data.name: Gopinath
data.long_meaning: Gopinath is a name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘go’ (cow) and ‘pana’ (to protect or to have). This name is associated with Lord Krishna, who is often depicted as the protector and shepherd of the cowherds. The name Gopinath signifies the one who looks after, protects, and cherishes his people, just as a cowherd takes care of his cattle.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes love, protection, and nurturing of the people.
data.numerology_meaning: People with the name Gopinath are caring, loving, and nurturing. They are known for their ability to provide comfort and support to those around them. Their natural generosity and compassion make them popular among friends and family. However, they can also be prone to self-doubt and insecurity, and may struggle with expressing their emotions.

data.cultural_impact: Gopinath is a revered name in Hindu culture, particularly in the state of Bengal, you'll often come across temples and shrines dedicated to this deity. Worship of Gopinath is deeply ingrained in the cultural practices of communities in India and Nepal, where people perform rituals to seek his blessings, ask for his protection, and express their devotion. Gopinath is also known for his association with Radha, the consort of Lord Krishna, emphasizing the divine love and companionship embodied in their union.
data.spiritual_significance: Gopinath represents a profound attachment to the divine and the natural world. The name denotes the transcendental presence of God within every living being, as well as in the realm of nature, particularly animals. By invoking the name Gopinath, one can tap into a deep sense of devotion and surrender, connecting with the ultimate shepherd who protects, nurtures, and guides us on our spiritual journey through life. Thus, the name Gopinath holds significant spiritual significance by reminding us of the divine protection and love that surrounds us.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Gopinath is a name of the Hindu god Vishnu, who is often depicted as a cowherd playing his flute. The name Gopinath carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Gopinath is a form of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to have appeared as a cowherd to his beloved Radha.
